summary: Gerlach Royen was a linguist who studied at Leiden University (Ph.D. under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck, c. 1918–1926). He taught at Gymnasium Immaculatae Conceptionis (1905–1911) and was extraordinary Professor of Comparative and General Linguistics at Utrecht University (1932–1943).
Gernot Böhme was a philosopher who studied at the University of Hamburg from c. 1961 to 1965. He held a position at the Technical University of Darmstadt from c. 1977 to 2002.

Gernot Rotter studied at the University of Tübingen (c. 1961–1965) and the University of Bonn (c. 1965–1967), where he was a student of Annemarie Schimmel. He later held a post at the University of Hamburg (c. 1984–2001).

Gernot Schmidt worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. under Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle at the Free University of Berlin (c. 1957–1962), studied at the University of Bonn, and became Professor of IE Linguistics there in 1980.

Gerrit Jan Held worked in Indology and anthropology. He earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong, was Professor of Cultural Anthropology at the University of Indonesia (1946–1950), and visited Yale University (1951–1952).

Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld was an Indology scholar who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (c. 1954–1974). From 1978 to 1986, he served as an associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen.

Gert Klingenschmitt specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his Ph.D. under Karl Hoffmann and his Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, later holding the Lehrstuhl für Indogermanistik at the University of Regensburg (1983–2006).

Geshe Gendun Lodro was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Khensur Ngawang Legden at Drepung Gomang Dratsang. He held positions at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg (1967), and the University of Virginia (1979).

Geshe Jampa Tegchok was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery (c. 1982–1993) and as resident teacher at Land of Medicine Buddha (c. 1998–2001).
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts attested at Gyume Tantric College in 1987 and at Sera Monastery in 1992.

Geshe Lhakdor is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Educated at the Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery, he served at Tibet House, New Delhi, and became Director of the LTWA in 2005.

Geshe Lhundup Sopa was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Gaden Chokhor and Sera Jey monasteries. He founded the Deer Park Buddhist Center in 1976 and taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, becoming full Professor in 1985.
Geshe Lobsang Tharchin was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Gyume Tantric College and Sera Monastery, where he earned the Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953.

Geshe Losang Chödar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 2010, he was attested holding posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics.

Geshe Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held appointments at Leiden University, served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery, and was attested at Drepung Monastery in 1966, 1976, and 1995.

Geshe Ngawang Samten is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar educated at CIHTS and Ganden Shartse Monastery. He was Chief Editor at CIHTS (c. 1985–2021) and held visiting roles at Smith, Amherst, and Hampshire colleges, and the University of Tasmania.
Geshe Palden Dragpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a post as Librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi, attested between 1987 and 1992, and was also attested there in 2004.

Geshe Palden Drakpa is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as Librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi, attested in 1988.

Geshe Rabten was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Trijang Rinpoche at Sera Monastery (c. 1940–1959). He taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (c. 1969–1974) and founded Rabten Choeling in 1977.

Geshe Sonam Rinchen was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and CIHTS, and became a resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives in 1978.
